concepts.def: Currency rises in value vs others.
Currency falls in value vs others.

walkthroughs.body_html: Rule: multiply when going from pounds to foreign; divide when coming back. Example: £200 × 1.20 = $240. To go back: $240 ÷ 1.20 = £200. Always double-check by reversing.
UK exports £450bn, imports £520bn. Trade balance = 450 − 520 = −£70bn deficit. A persistent deficit can weaken the £ over time as more pounds are sold to buy foreign currency for imports.

If £1 falls from $1.30 to $1.10, UK goods are 15% cheaper to American buyers — exports likely rise. But imported petrol and food cost more pounds — inflation rises. Evaluation: depends on PED of exports/imports.

mcqs.q: If the pound depreciates, UK exports become?
What are the functions of money?
options: Comparative advantage means richer countries should help poorer ones.
Medium of exchange, store of value, unit of account, and standard of deferred payment — money must perform these to function as money.
Money is only valuable if backed by gold.
Money is valuable because it is made of valuable materials.

mcqs.q: What components make up aggregate demand?
options: Aggregate demand is just the total amount consumers want to buy.
Money is only valuable if backed by gold.
Aggregate demand is the same as GDP measured by demand.
AD = C + I + G + (X - M): consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports. A shift in any component shifts the AD curve.

mcqs.q: What is the principle of comparative advantage?
options: Countries should specialise in producing goods with lower opportunity cost relative to others — even a country worse at everything still has a comparative advantage in something.
Money is only valuable if backed by gold.
Comparative advantage means richer countries should help poorer ones.
A country should produce whatever it can make best.
